chapter: Chapter 4 — Hostile Armies, More Magic and the Spoils of Victory

facts: The page opens in the middle of the sheep adventure: the sling stone had knocked out three or four of his teeth, and he fell from his horse stunned
The shepherds, believing they had killed him, whoever he was, gathered their sheep, collected the carcasses of those that had been killed, and moved along as fast as they could
Sancho Panza came running to the aid of his master, full of complaints and scolding him
Sancho said: Did I not tell you they were only sheep and you had no reason to meddle with them?
Don Quixote answered that the thief of an enchanter, his mortal enemy, can transform things or make them invisible
He said the enchanter envies the glory he would gain from battle so much that he transforms armies into flocks
Seeing the state of his master's mouth, Sancho went back to his donkey to get something from the pouches to clean it with
It was then he discovered, to his sadness, that the bags were missing
The innkeeper had taken the bags as payment, though Sancho had not noticed the loss during his hasty exit from the inn
Sancho vowed he would return home, abandoning his master, the wages he was owed, and his hopes of governing an island
When Don Quixote heard of the loss his dismay was nearly as great as his squire's, since to the immediate pangs of hunger was now added the prospect of starvation
He did the best he could to cheer his man, and they agreed their only course was to push on and find an inn where they could get food and lodging
Sancho said: And pray to heaven that there will not be any blanket-tossers, or spirits, or enchanted Moors there
Since they were on the high road they reasoned they must sooner or later come to an inn, but the way was long, they moved slowly, and night fell as they were still on the road
Suddenly they saw a great number of moving lights coming in their direction
Presently they saw these were carried by a vast throng of figures, dressed in white, who carried a black litter in their midst
Sancho immediately hid along the side of the road, but Don Quixote held his ground, determined to confront the spectral crowd
Don Quixote shouted: Ho! Knights! Halt! Whoever you are, tell me what you are carrying away, for either you are doing evil work or someone has done evil to you
He added: In either case, I am here to punish or avenge you

glossary.Moors: Arabs who crossed from Africa and held Spain as a Muslim country from 731 to 1492. They are admired for their contributions to art, architecture, and higher learning.
glossary.litter: A covered and curtained couch on poles in which one person was carried.

facts: One of the white figures in front, mounted on a mule, answered that they were in haste, for the nearest inn was still a long way off and they had no time to stop and answer him
Don Quixote said: Stand! And treat me with civility. Tell me what I demand or prepare for battle
As the man tried to push past him, Don Quixote grabbed the bridle of the mule, which immediately caused the mule to rear on its hind legs and threw the rider over to the ground
Another man came forward and began to yell at Don Quixote for his violence, which was more than the knight could bear
He lowered his lance and charged the crowd, drove one man to the ground, and turned to attack the others
But they, a cowardly lot, scattered in all directions, looking, with their white robes and torches, like masqueraders after a carnival
Don Quixote returned to the fallen man and, threatening him with his lance, demanded that he surrender
The man said: I am surrendered enough, seeing as my leg is broken and I cannot move. I beg you not to harm me more. I am in Holy Orders
The man began to explain that he and eleven other brothers were on an errand

glossary.Holy Orders: In the Catholic Church, Brothers of the Dominican Order, which emphasizes preaching, wear white.

facts: The man finished his explanation: he and eleven other brothers had come from Baeza to escort that casket, which contains the body of a gentleman they were taking to Segovia, his birthplace, for burial
Don Quixote asked: And who killed him?
The man answered: God, by a fever
Don Quixote said in a disappointed tone that there was nothing for him to set right
He told the man: You must know that I am Don Quixote de la Mancha, and it is my business to go about the world righting wrongs
The man begged him to right the wrong he had done to him by freeing his leg from under the mule
Don Quixote replied: Why did you not say so before? I might have gone on talking to you all night without finding out
He called Sancho to come help him, but the sensible and hungry squire was just then ransacking a pack mule that belonged to the funeral procession
Sancho had made his cloak into a sort of sack and was cramming it full with food
When he was done and the bundle was tied safely to his own donkey, he responded to his master's call
Very soon they had freed the trapped man, mounted him on his mule, and putting a torch in his hand, sent him on to rejoin his companions
Don Quixote wanted to stay to examine the casket, but Sancho persuaded him to leave at once so that they could find a peaceful place to eat the first food they had touched that day
They soon came to a secluded valley where they camped on fresh grass and made a hearty meal
But they found no wine among the monks' provisions, which greatly disappointed Sancho, and they did not even have water to wash down their food
Noticing how green the grass was, they concluded they must be near a spring or brook and set out in search of it
Soon they heard the sound of falling waters and hurried in its direction
But as they went farther they also heard other sounds, heavy blows at regular intervals with the clanging of iron and rattling of chains
They stopped to listen, but could not understand the noise
The hour was late and the night was pitch black, and they were in the midst of lofty trees whose high leaves made strange whisperings
The place was solitary and mysterious, and filled now with fear, Sancho began trembling
But Don Quixote, mounted on Rocinante, took up his lance and shield and announced that he was going on to explore the haunted glen
He told Sancho to tighten the saddle and then gave him some final instructions
His instruction was: Wait here three days, and if at the end of that time I do not return, go home to our village and then to Toboso
